reviews.text:
Pretty but database is lacking, pro details nonexistent. I've downloaded several food tracker apps to use and compare. I'm willing to pay for Pro service if it offers the right features at the right price, I'm not expecting to get everything I want for free. 

That said, the reviews for ARISE made me hopeful, as did the beautiful interface and integration with HealthKit. But when I tried to add my first food item I discovered the database is horribly incomplete. 

Only very basic food items are included, such as "Chips." So I tried adding something every other app's database includes a "ThinkThin Creamy Peanut Butter Bar." Nothing came up. I tried "ThinkThin"... nothing. I tried "Think thin"... I get 1 hit for "Think thin Barry (sic) oatmeal." (Apparently it's a user-added food, and since it's hand-typed and misspelled I'd be hesitant to trust the data.) There's no scanner so I have to manually enter the item. The app allows me to enter quantity in oz only, not "bar" or "g" and I can't enter 2.1 oz because there's no decimal option for that field. Further, I can only enter Protein, Carbs, and Fat. So... what if I'm trying to track net carbs? Do I input that instead? But my entry goes into the app's public (user) database and the field is labeled "Carbs" not "Net Carbs." In other words, user added food data isn't likely to be accurate or reliable. 

I don't know if an upgraded food database is included in the Pro subscription because there are no details as to what's included with Pro, only weight loss promises. The Developer's website is not in English, with no option to switch languages. 

After actually using this app I'm sorry to say I don't trust all the positive "reviews." I give it a Big Thumbs Down.
